---
title: "A2.2 Polynomial IVs with factor syntax"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_gss", clear

regress occprest c.age##c.age i.woman i.college
<</dd_do>>
```

Stata makes it easy to put in quadratic transformations of your independent variables. Make sure to use the "**c.**" prefix so Stata knows it is a continuous variable, then add **\##** between the variable---this tells Stata to estimate a linear term (*age*) and a quadratic term (*age^2^*)

### Plotting predictions

- The code for making predictions when you have a quadratic term in the model is the **exact same** as before in the linear case if you use the proper **c.** and **i.** prefixes and specify quadratics using **\##**

```stata
regress occprest c.age##c.age i.woman i.college

qui margins, at(age=(20(5)90))

marginsplot, ///
    title("Predicted Occupational Prestige Based on Person's Age") ///
    subtitle("Quadratic Term for Age", size(small)) ///
    ytitle("Occupational Prestige") ///
    recastci(rarea) ylab(38(2)46)
```
